name: Raw eggs / oysters / zinc-rich foods

lead: Some people eat oysters, raw eggs and other zinc-rich foods hoping to raise testosterone.
Reference texts say zinc is needed to make testosterone and deficiency lowers it, but that extra zinc beyond adequacy does not change serum levels.

paras: Zinc is required for testosterone production, so correcting a shortfall may restore levels [2]. Oysters are an unusually zinc-dense food [2].
The sources reviewed describe no harms from zinc-rich foods. Raw eggs and raw shellfish are not addressed in them.

lead: Raw eggs, oysters and other zinc-rich foods are eaten by some people in the belief that they raise testosterone. The reasoning rests mainly on zinc, a mineral needed to produce testosterone.

Wikipedia reports that zinc deficiency can lower circulating testosterone, and that over-supplementing zinc has no effect on serum testosterone levels [1][2]. Oysters are described as the richest dietary source of zinc by far [2]. The sources reviewed do not address raw eggs.
infobox: Effect seen in deficiency; no benefit reported with excess supplementation

paras: Zinc is required to produce testosterone, and deficiency can reduce levels, potentially leading to hypogonadism and delayed puberty [2]. A 1963 case report described a young man whose stunted growth and underdeveloped genitalia reversed with zinc supplementation [2]. The testosterone article similarly says zinc deficiency lowers testosterone, but over-supplementation does not change serum levels [1].

A 3-ounce serving of fried oysters is reported to contain about 74 mg of zinc, compared with about 7 mg in the same amount of braised beef chuck; other sources include crab, beef, cashews, lobster, pork and almonds [2]. Phytates in whole grains can reduce zinc absorption [2].
